newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper settles firmer, stock dip expected.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper settles firmer, stock dip expected.

text.p: COMEX copper settled firmer in generally lackluster trading ahead of an expected dip in LME stocks Tuesday.
Traders said LME stocks were set to fall by 2,000 to 4,000 tonnes.
Much of the upward momentum in copper was due to the generally bullish tone in the LME base metals complex overall, with strong gains in nickel, aluminum and zinc leading the way, traders added.
May COMEX copper settled 1.85 cents firmer at 112.75 cents per pound, traded 113.70 to 111.40 cents. Spot March went out 1.80 cents up at 115.55 cents.
March hit 116.00 cents briefly, the highest for the spot month since mid-June 1996.
Volume was estimated at 9,000 lots compared to Friday's estimated 9,689 lots.
Spending on U.S. construction, a key copper consuming sector, in January rose 0.4 percent, up from a revised dip of 0.9 percent in December.
